story.sq08.title: A Bowl Kept for No One
story.sq08.summary: Read Mei’s unfinished picnic plan and help Lan make room for an ordinary meal without pretending grief is finished.
story.sq08.s1.objective: Read the folded recipe beneath the old table’s empty bowl.
story.sq08.s1.journal: The folded page is a plan for a picnic, not a final message. Mei complained about salty broth, invited Wen, and crossed out her own exaggerated boast. Lan has kept a place as if the meal could still happen unchanged.
story.sq08.s1.lan: She hated the little bowl. Said it cooled before she finished talking. I keep putting it out because the table looks wrong without it. I know she is not coming.
story.sq08.s1.apprentice: We can keep the recipe without keeping a seat waiting. Would you like to show me where she planned to eat?
story.sq08.s1.note: Mei’s picnic plan, one week before the White Tide: “Rice broth, less salt. Ask Wen for the sour greens recipe, not the greens—she will think I am borrowing supper again. Bring the wide bowl. Lan will forget spoons, so pack two. After lunch, show him the new shelf route. I am the best guide in the valley [crossed out]. I am the guide who remembered spoons.”
story.sq08.s2.objective: At the safe picnic shelf, read the margin note and choose where the recipe copy belongs.
story.sq08.s2.journal: A later margin says she wanted the route checked before bringing children. I can leave a recipe copy at the communal table or add it to the field workers’ meal book. The original stays in Lan’s care. Neither choice moves the working spillway lamp.
story.sq08.s2.lan: She was impatient with everyone, including me. I do not need you to tell me every word she wrote was wise. The spoon joke still makes me cross. Then it makes me laugh.
story.sq08.s2.clue: The margin belongs to the same living week, not to a message from beyond death: “Check the shelf after rain. No picnic is worth carrying a child over a broken rail.” Inspect the existing rail and dry marker; this visit does not replace SQ01’s full spillway test.
story.sq08.s2.choice_a: Copy the recipe for the communal table.
story.sq08.s2.choice_b: Copy the recipe for the field workers’ meal book.
story.sq08.s2.reply_a: Anyone using the table can try it. I will keep the crossed-out boast; it sounds like someone, not an inscription.
story.sq08.s2.reply_b: Workers can pack the wide bowl and the extra spoon. The copy will say whose practical complaint started it.
story.sq08.s3.objective: Return to the table, place the recipe copy, and share the prepared meal with Lan.
story.sq08.s3.journal: This meal requires no ingredient hunt. The pantry already has enough for two. Lan can put away the waiting bowl without throwing away Mei’s page. I do not need to persuade him that he has healed.
story.sq08.s3.lan: Not that small bowl. Take the wide one. I put too much salt in again. She would have complained before the first spoonful.
story.sq08.s3.apprentice: There is water to thin it. We can sit while it cools.
story.sq08.s3.record: Recipe copy placed at the selected site. Original returned to Lan. The small waiting bowl is stored, not broken. The shared meal is recorded as an ordinary present-day meal; no voice, soul, or answering echo appears. Mei’s page remains a person’s unfinished plan.
story.sq08.s3.confirm: Sit down and share the meal.
story.sq08.s3.retry: The recipe copy has not been placed or the table interaction is unfinished. Return whenever you are ready; no pantry item is consumed before confirmation.
story.sq08.s3.done: The meal is finished. The original page stays with Lan; the copy is available at its chosen site.
story.sq08.epilogue.open: During the apprentice’s first long watch, Lan brings broth in a wide bowl. He still talks about Mei, sometimes with anger, sometimes with a joke. No one asks him to be finished grieving.
story.sq08.epilogue.seal: Lan packs the recipe with the tools leaving the retired sanctuary. At the alternative channel’s table, he complains about the salt before anyone else can. The small bowl stays safely wrapped.
story.sq08.epilogue.shared: After the first shared-maintenance shift, the rota leaves time for a meal. Someone forgets spoons. Lan laughs, then fetches the spare pair himself. Mei has not returned; something she cared about is still used.
